basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Hic erit ferus homo, manus ejus contra omnes, et manus omnium contra eum, et e regione'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Hic erit ferus homo, manus ejus contra omnes, et manus omnium contra eum, et e regione universorum fratrum suorum figet tabernacula. Significat semen ejus habitaturum in eremo, id est, Saracenos vagos, incertisque sedibus, qui universas gentes quibus desertum ex latere jungitur incursant, et expugnantur ab omnibus: sed haec antiquitus. Nunc autem in tantum manus ejus contra omnes, et manus sunt omnium contra eum; ut Africam totam in longitudine sua ditione premant, sed et Asiae maximam partem, et Europae nonnullam omnibus exosi et contrarii teneant. Quod autem dicit: Figet tabernacula; morem gentis antiquum ostendit, quae in tabernaculis semper, non in domibus, habitare solebat.
